fact: 1917年2月1日，德国恢复无限制潜艇战。协约国与中立国船舶损失随即急剧上升，1917年4月达到881,027吨，为战时单月最高（另一口径作「超过85万吨」）；此后随着反制措施生效，世界船舶月损失到9月回落到30万吨以下。

sources.title: University of Warwick, CAGE Working Paper 750: Blockading Britain and Germany during World War 1
sources.quote: Unrestricted submarine warfare was declared in January 2017 and the campaign began on 1 February. Initially, German sinkings of Allied and neutral shipping increased dramatically ... peaking at over 850,000 tons in April 1917. ... After reaching a peak of 881,000 tons in April 1917, world total sinkings fell back under 300,000 tons by September

sources.title: The Strategy Bridge, Death from Below, Salvation from Above
sources.quote: the British and their allies lost 881,027 tons of shipping that month (including those losses not due to submarine activity), which represents an increase of 287,186 compared to the previous month

fact: 1917年4月底至5月，英国海军部在首相劳合·乔治的压力下开始实行护航制，5月10日首次大规模护航编队出航。1917年5月10日至1918年11月23日，共有16,693艘船在护航编队中航行，其中99.08%安全抵达，仅0.61%在编队中被鱼雷击沉；世界船舶月损失从4月的88.1万吨降到9月的30万吨以下。

sources.title: University of Warwick, CAGE Working Paper 750
sources.quote: The effectiveness of the convoy system is demonstrated by the statistics on convoy sailings and losses in Table 3. Of 16,693 ships sailing in convoys on both homewards and outwards voyages between 10 May 1917 and 23 November 1918, 99.08 per cent were escorted safely, with just 0.61 per cent torpedoed in convoy.

sources.title: The Strategy Bridge, Death from Below, Salvation from Above
sources.quote: three days before the Prime Minister's visit, the Admiralty had given orders to begin a trial convoy from Gibraltar.

fact: 1917年9月，英国政府把4磅重面包的价格从1先令（或1先令1便士）压到9便士，差额由政府补贴支付；同时自9月3日起以食品管制令规定最高零售价：面粉每石不超过3先令6便士，4磅面包不超过9便士，2磅4.5便士，1磅2.5便士。这是英国从自愿节约转向价格管制的节点。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1922, Volume 31, p.111（Wikisource 全文，Food Supply 条）
sources.quote: In Sept. 1917 the price of bread was lowered from 1s. or 1s. 1d. to 9d. for the quartern loaf, the difference being paid by the Government as a subsidy. At about the same time there was fixed a scale of prices for meat and for live stock

sources.title: Great War Forum, price of loaf of bread 1914-18（转录当时报刊与法庭记录）
sources.quote: September 1917. The introduction of a wide range of Food Control Orders was announced, with effect from September 3rd maximum retail prices were fixed by the Food Controller. Floor was to be sold at no more than 3/6d. a stone ... Bread was to be no more than 9d. for a 4 lb. loaf, 4½d. per 2 lb. loaf and 2½d. per 1 lb. loaf.

fact: 1917年2月，英国政府呼吁民众把面包消费限制在每人每周4磅，5月国王发表公告要求少吃面包，公告在每教区宣读。1917年英国始终没有实行强制面包配给，强制配给要到1918年初才逐步推开。1917年6月收到的工业动荡专员报告，把物价上涨与食糖分配不善列为动乱的两个首要原因。

sources.title: Everyday Lives in War（University of Hertfordshire）, Bread and War
sources.quote: The government hoped to control the food situation through voluntary action and in February 1917 it appealed to citizens to restrict themselves to four pounds of bread a week. The King himself exhorted the population to eat less bread in a royal proclamation of May 1917, a document read from the pulpit in every parish.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1922, Volume 31, p.111
sources.quote: Meanwhile, the people themselves were mainly disturbed by the rise of prices and the bad distribution of sugar. The reports of the Commissioners on Industrial Unrest, received in June 1917, emphasized these two points above all as the causes of unrest. ... how the ensuing shortage, aggravated by large purchases of home-grown meat for the army and by other circumstances, was dealt with by rationing in the early part of 1918

fact: 英国4磅面包的价格从1914年7月的5.5便士涨到1915年7月的8便士、1916年7月的9便士、1917年3月的11便士，到1917年春达到1先令，正好是战前的两倍；1917年9月补贴后回落到9便士。以1914年7月为100，英国零售食品价格指数1917年年均为198，12月为205，即食品价格约为战前的两倍。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1922, Prices 条（Labour Gazette 零售食品价格表）
sources.quote: The price of bread rose intermittently, but on the whole rapidly till Sept. 1917, when its price was exactly double that of July 1914. ... Average for year — 131 160 198 215 219 256

sources.title: Great War Forum, price of loaf of bread 1914-18（引 1917 年议会辩论数据）
sources.quote: The price of the 4lb. loaf has risen from 5½d. in July 1914 to 8d. in July 1915, 9d. in July 1916, and 11d. in March 1917. Thus in the most important article of consumption the rise has been exactly 100 per cent.

fact: 1917年英国的食品价格管制以《领土防卫法》（DORA）下的食品管制令执行，违者按刑事程序起诉。1917年9月，霍姆弗斯（Holmfirth）一名马铃薯商因售价高于食品管制官规定的价格被罚款10先令并付2先令6便士诉讼费；同月一家杂货店因李子酱每2磅超价5便士被起诉。价格管制同时适用于面粉、面包、肉、果酱等，违反者多为小店主。

sources.title: Great War Forum, price of loaf of bread 1914-18（转录 Holmfirth 治安法庭 1917 年 9 月记录）
sources.quote: October 13th 1917. Mr. Herbert Heeley appeared at Holmfirth Police Court charged with selling potatoes at a price that was above the rate specified by the Government Food Controller. ... The Magistrates imposed a fine of ten shillings with two shillings and sixpence costs. ... charged with selling plum jam at a price exceeding the maximum price stipulated by the Food Controller, in contravention of the Jam Prices Order 1917, a regulation under the Defence of the Realm Act.

fact: 1917年1月12日，英国发行「5%战争公债」：5%公债按95发行、需缴所得税，另有4%免税公债按面值发行，并允许持有人把旧债转换。认购期五周，2月16日截止，认购人数5,289,000人，总额1,000,312,950英镑，其中新增资金逾9.6亿英镑；这是当时英国乃至任何国家最大的一次融资。1917年10月又推出不限额、持续销售的「国民战争债券」，至1919年1月11日售出14.466亿英镑。

sources.title: Bank of England Archive, 5% War Loan 1929-1947 and 4% War Loan 1929-1942 - issued Jan 1917
sources.quote: The loan consisted of two distinct issues: a 5% War Loan 1929-1947 at 95 subject to Income Tax ... and a 4% War Loan 1929-1942 at 100 free of income tax ... The prospectus for both loans was issued on the 12th January 1917. ... The total new money obtained during the five weeks was over £960,347,000 ... The aggregate total of the two loans was £2,127,985,066

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1922, Law, Andrew Bonar 条
sources.quote: The first loan was launched in Jan. 1917, and its basis was the issue of a 5% Government stock at 95 ... It brought in the enormous sum of £1,000,312,950 from no fewer than 5,289,000 subscribers ... From the time they were first put on sale till Jan. 11 1919, £1,446,625,613 of these bonds were sold

fact: 1917年11月20日晨6时，英军第三集团军在康布雷发起进攻，投入476辆马克IV型坦克（其中378辆用于作战），这是战争开始以来最大规模的坦克集中使用。首日英军推进约5英里并夺取数个村庄，但当天结束时有超过一半的坦克失去战斗力；到12月7日战役结束，英军伤亡约4.4万人，战果大多被德军反攻夺回。

sources.title: Imperial War Museums, How the Battle of Cambrai changed fighting tactics on the Western Front
sources.quote: At dawn on 20 November 1917, the British Third Army launched an attack towards Cambrai ... The Battle of Cambrai was the first large-scale use of massed tanks in battle. ... In total, the British deployed 476 tanks at Cambrai, including 378 in combat roles. ... British forces made advances of around 5 miles ... But by the end of the first day, over half of the tanks were out of action.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Battle of Cambrai (1917)
sources.quote: Date 20 November – 7 December 1917 ... 476 tanks (378 combat tanks) ... Casualties and losses 44,207 (c. 6,000 POW)

fact: 1917年英国的食品进口与批发被国家接管到前所未有的程度：粮食与糖由两个皇家委员会进口，培根、火腿、奶酪、黄油、食用油、炼乳、罐头肉、蛋、茶乃至苹果、橙子、果酱与干果，均由食品部直接进口或在到港后征用；本国出产的肉、奶酪与大部分黄油也经食品部之手。到战争末期，平民消费的食品中有85%由食品部买进卖出，食品部年营业额接近9亿英镑。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1922, Volume 31, p.111（Food Supply 条）
sources.quote: Under Lord Rhondda all bacon, ham, lard, cheese, butter and similar provisions, all oils and fats ... brought into this country, came to be directly imported by the Ministry of Food or requisitioned on arrival. ... Ultimately 85% of all the food consumed by civilians in Great Britain was actually bought and sold by the Ministry of Food. ... The total turnover of the Ministry's trading (including the two Royal Commissions) was nearly £900,000,000 a year.
